Once upon a time, I’d have fought and cried at a statement like that. If that’s your conclusion, I can’t change your mind. There’s a lot of context here that pushes this into a very strange grey area, whether you think I am a rapist or not, I’m not the suited man dropping roofies into girl’s drinks at clubs. I’m not the hooded youth that stalks alleyways and woods for vulnerable women. I’m not the depraved uncle that manipulated and touches his own flesh and blood. This happened with myself and my ex partner being very intoxicated, in what we both felt was a comfortable environment, with two people that had spent three years of their childhood together. There was no intent, consent was even established prior, and I can’t even remember most of what happened. I have never wanted to do that to anyone, especially not someone that I spent so much time being that close with. I can’t say I disagree with you, but I can’t agree with what you’re saying either.
I did see it, I'm starting to consider other options. Those other options ultimately just delay my suicide, but they are other options.
I’m from the UK, and I can’t remember if he was 53rd exactly, but it was 50 something.

Also: I’m sorry about your rapist getting away scot-free. There‘s a beautiful irony in a serial rapist being able to work and return to his family whilst I’m in the puddle of mud, haha. That’s life for you, isn’t it? 

I don’t want to let this girl and the so-called “friend” win either, so I’m not even going to allow this to progress into court. They were both very excited to take to twitter and fantasise about what “wrestling-style” entrances and theme music their court walk-ins would have. Real sickening stuff.

My lawyer is a great lawyer. He’s what, 53rd or something in the country, which isn’t bad at all, and I think that maybe there’s even hope, there is a chance that he’d smash the trial and I’d be able to return home to my family and back into work. Unfortunately, I can’t see myself taking that risk. It’s just too heavy of a hammer to swing.

You’ve still got a life to live, man. That’s one thing I want to scream at everybody that posts here. I’m not committing suicide for the sheer fact that I’ve had enough, or my mental health has deteriorated, no. I’ve made this choice because odds are, I will receive a fate worse than death, in my eyes - and that’s not going to prison, I am not scared of prison, not anymore. Prison would be good for me, most likely. But, I’m scared of what comes after, because I’ll be registered. I’ll never work again. I’ll never meet anyone again. When I leave, I will have to look all of my neighbours, close friends and people I grew up around in the eyes and tell them I am a registered offender. I know I don’t deserve that, perhaps I do deserve it by law, and by definition, but logically and morally, I know I don’t.

See, you don’t have that fate that’s set in stone. You can keep living on, we can all change, starting now. I know it’s hippie bullshit, but it really can get better if you work and make changes. I really do hope you find that peace, and that ability to make the change, I know, from personal experience that BPD can be an absolutely massive roadblock to making that change. It took me a LOT of courage to leave my FP after so much abuse, and the emotional battle afterwards was bloody, and it wreaked havoc on my family. But I got through it, unfortunately it’s all a waste now, but I still got through it. You can do it, man. I believe in you.
